# BMI -> systolic blood pressure: two-sample MR (simulated data)

Implements `analysis_plan.md` in base R. Data dictionary: `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

## Rerun
From this folder:

    conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript analysis/mr_analysis.R data/main

(The dataset folder argument is optional; default is `data/main`.) Outputs:
`results/estimates.csv`, `results/harmonisation_log.csv`, `results/figures/scatter.png`.
The script also regenerates a basic `report.md`, overwriting the hand-edited version; the
edited report is the one for the group, so keep a copy before rerunning.

## Test
    conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript tests/test_known_answer.R

Simulates exposure and outcome files covering every allele situation (aligned, swapped, complemented,
complemented and swapped, palindromic on same/opposite strand, plus dropped cases) with a true effect of
2 mmHg per kg/m2 (plus a four-variant example with hand-calculated answers), runs the script and checks the log labels and that IVW, MR-Egger and weighted median recover it.

## Headline result
89 of 100 instruments used. IVW estimate: **0.21 mmHg SBP per 1 kg/m2 BMI (95% CI 0.15 to 0.26)**.
Weighted median 0.23 (0.14 to 0.32); MR-Egger 0.32 (0.15 to 0.49), intercept -0.016 (-0.039 to 0.007).
Cochran's Q = 89.9 (df 88, p = 0.42), so there is no evidence of heterogeneity. The direction is positive in all methods
and all intervals exclude zero. Data are simulated.

Correction: an earlier version did not negate the outcome effect for variants whose outcome alleles are the
complement of the exposure alleles with order swapped (27 variants, now labelled
"strand: complemented and allele order swapped, flipped"). This had biased the IVW estimate towards zero (previously 1.59).

Correction 2: exposure BETA and SE (per SD of BMI) were divided by 4.8 instead of multiplied, so every causal
estimate was 4.8² ≈ 23 times too large (IVW had been 4.77). The known-answer test had the same error in its data
generation, so it passed anyway; it now also includes a hand-worked example (expected IVW 0.5, SE 1/12).
# BMI and systolic blood pressure: Mendelian randomization (simulated data)

**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.

**Data.** 100 BMI instruments; 89 used. Dropped: 4 absent from the outcome GWAS, 3 with missing outcome data, 4 ambiguous palindromic variants (MAF > 0.42). Details: `results/harmonisation_log.csv`. An earlier version mishandled variants whose outcome alleles were complemented and swapped (27 variants); this is corrected, which changed the results. A second error is also corrected: exposure effects were divided by 4.8 instead of multiplied (BETA is per SD, 1 SD = 4.8 kg/m2), which made every estimate 4.8² ≈ 23 times too large.

**Results (mmHg per kg/m2).**
- IVW (random effects): 0.21 (95% CI 0.15 to 0.26)
- Weighted median: 0.23 (95% CI 0.14 to 0.32)
- MR-Egger: 0.32 (95% CI 0.15 to 0.49)

All estimates are positive and all intervals exclude zero. MR-Egger is the least precise and its point estimate is the largest.

**Heterogeneity and pleiotropy.** Cochran's Q = 89.9 on 88 df (p = 0.42): no evidence of heterogeneity. MR-Egger intercept = -0.016 mmHg (95% CI -0.039 to 0.007): no clear directional pleiotropy.

**Caveats.** Results rest on MR assumptions these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings.

     1	#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
     2	# Two-sample MR: effect of BMI on systolic blood pressure (mmHg per 1 kg/m2).
     3	# Implements analysis_plan.md using base R only.
     4	# Usage (from the project root): Rscript analysis/mr_analysis.R [dataset_folder]
     5	# Default dataset folder: data/main. Outputs go to results/ and report.md in the working directory.
     6	
     7	args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
     8	data_dir <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else "data/main"
     9	
    10	SD_BMI_KGM2  <- 4.8    # 1 SD of BMI in kg/m2 (data dictionary)
    11	MAF_MAX_PAL  <- 0.42   # palindromic variants with MAF above this are dropped
    12	MISSING_CODE <- -9     # outcome missing-value code
    13	set.seed(20240601)     # for the weighted-median bootstrap
    14	
    15	dir.create("results/figures", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    16	
    17	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. Read and clean
    18	exp_file <- file.path(data_dir, "exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv")
    19	out_file <- file.path(data_dir, "outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv")
    20	stopifnot(file.exists(exp_file), file.exists(out_file))
    21	
    22	exposure <- read.delim(exp_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
    23	outcome  <- read.delim(out_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
    24	
    25	# -9 is the outcome's missing code (numeric columns; also guard allele columns)
    26	for (v in c("chr", "pos", "freq", "beta", "se", "pval", "n")) {
    27	  if (v %in% names(outcome)) {
    28	    outcome[[v]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(outcome[[v]]))
    29	    outcome[[v]][!is.na(outcome[[v]]) & outcome[[v]] == MISSING_CODE] <- NA
    30	  }
    31	}
    32	for (v in c("A1", "A2")) outcome[[v]][outcome[[v]] %in% as.character(MISSING_CODE)] <- NA
    33	outcome$A1 <- toupper(outcome$A1); outcome$A2 <- toupper(outcome$A2)
    34	exposure$EFFECT_ALLELE <- toupper(exposure$EFFECT_ALLELE)
    35	exposure$OTHER_ALLELE  <- toupper(exposure$OTHER_ALLELE)
    36	
    37	if (anyDuplicated(exposure$SNP)) stop("Duplicate SNP ids in exposure file")
    38	if (anyDuplicated(outcome$rsid)) stop("Duplicate rsid in outcome file")
    39	
    40	dat <- merge(exposure, outcome, by.x = "SNP", by.y = "rsid", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
    41	dat <- dat[match(exposure$SNP, dat$SNP), ]   # keep exposure order
    42	
    43	in_outcome  <- dat$SNP %in% outcome$rsid
    44	usable_out  <- in_outcome & !is.na(dat$beta) & !is.na(dat$se) & dat$se > 0 &
    45	               !is.na(dat$A1) & !is.na(dat$A2)
    46	
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Harmonise
    48	# Target: outcome effect expressed for the exposure effect allele (EA).
    49	comp <- function(a) c(A = "T", T = "A", C = "G", G = "C")[a]
    50	is_pal <- function(a, b) paste0(sort(c(a, b)), collapse = "") %in% c("AT", "CG")
    51	
    52	dat$action <- NA_character_
    53	dat$flip   <- NA     # TRUE: outcome beta must be negated and freq -> 1 - freq
    54	dat$out_freq_ea <- NA_real_   # outcome frequency of the exposure EA after harmonisation
    55	
    56	for (i in seq_len(nrow(dat))) {
    57	  if (!in_outcome[i]) { dat$action[i] <- "dropped: not in outcome GWAS"; next }
    58	  if (!usable_out[i]) { dat$action[i] <- "dropped: outcome data missing (-9)"; next }
    59	
    60	  ea <- dat$EFFECT_ALLELE[i]; oa <- dat$OTHER_ALLELE[i]
    61	  a1 <- dat$A1[i];            a2 <- dat$A2[i]
    62	  if (!all(c(ea, oa, a1, a2) %in% c("A", "C", "G", "T"))) {
    63	    dat$action[i] <- "dropped: non-ACGT or indel alleles"; next
    64	  }
    65	  # outcome effect is for A2; frequency of EA in outcome if strands agree
    66	  if (is_pal(ea, oa)) {
    67	    if (!(a1 == ea && a2 == oa) && !(a1 == oa && a2 == ea)) {
    68	      dat$action[i] <- "dropped: allele mismatch"; next
    69	    }
    70	    eaf <- dat$EAF[i]
    71	    f_naive <- if (a2 == ea) dat$freq[i] else 1 - dat$freq[i]   # assumes same strand
    72	    if (is.na(eaf) || is.na(f_naive) ||
    73	        min(eaf, 1 - eaf) > MAF_MAX_PAL ||
    74	        min(dat$freq[i], 1 - dat$freq[i]) > MAF_MAX_PAL) {
    75	      dat$action[i] <- "dropped: palindromic, MAF > 0.42 (strand ambiguous)"; next
    76	    }
    77	    same_strand <- (eaf < 0.5) == (f_naive < 0.5)
    78	    if (same_strand) {
    79	      dat$flip[i] <- (a2 != ea)
    80	      dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- f_naive
    81	      dat$action[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), flipped"
    82	                       else "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), no flip"
    83	    } else {
    84	      # opposite strand: outcome A2 is the complement of the allele it appears to be
    85	      dat$flip[i] <- (a2 == ea)
    86	      dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- 1 - f_naive
    87	      dat$action[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), flipped"
    88	                       else "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), no flip"
    89	    }
    90	    next
    91	  }
    92	  # non-palindromic
    93	  if (a2 == ea && a1 == oa) {
    94	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "none: alleles aligned"
    95	  } else if (a2 == oa && a1 == ea) {
    96	    dat$flip[i] <- TRUE;  dat$action[i] <- "flipped: allele order swapped"
    97	  } else if (a2 == comp(ea) && a1 == comp(oa)) {
    98	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented, no flip"
    99	  } else if (a2 == comp(oa) && a1 == comp(ea)) {
   100	    dat$flip[i] <- TRUE;  dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented and allele order swapped, flipped"
   101	  } else {
   102	    dat$action[i] <- "dropped: allele mismatch"; next
   103	  }
   104	  dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) 1 - dat$freq[i] else dat$freq[i]
   105	}
   106	
   107	dat$used <- !is.na(dat$flip)
   108	dat$beta_out_h <- ifelse(dat$used, ifelse(dat$flip, -dat$beta, dat$beta), NA)
   109	
   110	harm_log <- data.frame(
   111	  SNP = dat$SNP, exposure_EA = dat$EFFECT_ALLELE, exposure_OA = dat$OTHER_ALLELE,
   112	  exposure_EAF = dat$EAF, outcome_A1 = dat$A1, outcome_A2 = dat$A2,
   113	  outcome_freq_A2 = dat$freq, harmonisation_action = dat$action, used = dat$used,
   114	  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   115	write.csv(harm_log, "results/harmonisation_log.csv", row.names = FALSE)
   116	
   117	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Units
   118	# Exposure effects in kg/m2 per allele: BETA is in SD units, 1 SD = 4.8 kg/m2, so multiply.
   119	# Outcome already in mmHg; MR estimates are therefore mmHg per kg/m2.
   120	mr <- dat[dat$used, ]
   121	bx  <- mr$BETA * SD_BMI_KGM2
   122	sex <- mr$SE   * SD_BMI_KGM2
   123	by  <- mr$beta_out_h
   124	sey <- mr$se
   125	n   <- length(bx)
   126	if (n < 4) stop("Too few usable instruments (", n, ") for MR-Egger")
   127	cat(sprintf("%d of %d variants used\n", n, nrow(dat)))
   128	
   129	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. Estimate
   130	z975 <- qnorm(0.975)
   131	
   132	# IVW, multiplicative random effects (residual SE scaled, not allowed below 1)
   133	w <- 1 / sey^2
   134	ivw_fit <- lm(by ~ 0 + bx, weights = w)
   135	ivw_b   <- unname(coef(ivw_fit))
   136	sigma_i <- summary(ivw_fit)$sigma
   137	ivw_se  <- sqrt(1 / sum(w * bx^2)) * max(1, sigma_i)
   138	Q       <- sum(w * (by - ivw_b * bx)^2)
   139	Q_df    <- n - 1
   140	Q_p     <- pchisq(Q, Q_df, lower.tail = FALSE)
   141	I2      <- max(0, (Q - Q_df) / Q)
   142	
   143	# MR-Egger: orient so every SNP-exposure effect is positive
   144	sgn <- sign(bx); sgn[sgn == 0] <- 1
   145	bx_o <- bx * sgn; by_o <- by * sgn
   146	eg_fit  <- lm(by_o ~ bx_o, weights = w)
   147	eg_sum  <- summary(eg_fit)
   148	eg_sig  <- max(1, eg_sum$sigma)
   149	eg_coef <- eg_sum$coefficients
   150	eg_df   <- n - 2
   151	eg_int  <- eg_coef[1, 1]; eg_int_se <- eg_coef[1, 2] / eg_sum$sigma * eg_sig
   152	eg_b    <- eg_coef[2, 1]; eg_b_se   <- eg_coef[2, 2] / eg_sum$sigma * eg_sig
   153	tcrit   <- qt(0.975, eg_df)
   154	
   155	# Weighted median (Bowden 2016), first-order weights, parametric bootstrap SE
   156	wmedian <- function(b, wt) {
   157	  o <- order(b); b <- b[o]; wt <- wt[o] / sum(wt)
   158	  p <- cumsum(wt) - 0.5 * wt
   159	  below <- max(which(p < 0.5))
   160	  b[below] + (b[below + 1] - b[below]) * (0.5 - p[below]) / (p[below + 1] - p[below])
   161	}
   162	ratio    <- by / bx
   163	se_ratio <- sey / abs(bx)
   164	wm_b <- wmedian(ratio, 1 / se_ratio^2)
   165	boot <- replicate(1000, {
   166	  bxs <- rnorm(n, bx, sex); bys <- rnorm(n, by, sey)
   167	  wmedian(bys / bxs, 1 / (sey / abs(bxs))^2)
   168	})
   169	wm_se <- sd(boot)
   170	
   171	estimates <- data.frame(
   172	  method   = c("IVW (multiplicative random effects)", "MR-Egger", "MR-Egger intercept", "Weighted median"),
   173	  estimate = c(ivw_b, eg_b, eg_int, wm_b),
   174	  se       = c(ivw_se, eg_b_se, eg_int_se, wm_se),
   175	  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   176	crit <- c(z975, tcrit, tcrit, z975)
   177	estimates$ci_lower <- estimates$estimate - crit * estimates$se
   178	estimates$ci_upper <- estimates$estimate + crit * estimates$se
   179	estimates$n_snps   <- n
   180	estimates <- estimates[, c("method", "estimate", "se", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "n_snps")]
   181	write.csv(estimates, "results/estimates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
   182	
   183	cat(sprintf("IVW Cochran's Q = %.2f (df %d, p = %.3g), I2 = %.2f\n", Q, Q_df, Q_p, I2))
   184	print(estimates, digits = 4)
   185	
   186	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. Scatter plot
   187	png("results/figures/scatter.png", width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 200)
   188	xlim <- range(c(0, bx_o - z975 * sex, bx_o + z975 * sex))
   189	ylim <- range(c(by_o - z975 * sey, by_o + z975 * sey, 0))
   190	plot(bx_o, by_o, pch = 16, col = "grey30", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim,
   191	     xlab = "SNP effect on BMI (kg/m2 per allele)",
   192	     ylab = "SNP effect on SBP (mmHg per allele)",
   193	     main = "BMI -> SBP: SNP-outcome vs SNP-exposure effects")
   194	segments(bx_o, by_o - z975 * sey, bx_o, by_o + z975 * sey, col = "grey70")
   195	segments(bx_o - z975 * sex, by_o, bx_o + z975 * sex, by_o, col = "grey70")
   196	abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 3, col = "grey80")
   197	abline(0, ivw_b, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
   198	abline(eg_int, eg_b, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
   199	abline(0, wm_b, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
   200	legend("topleft", bty = "n", lwd = 2,
   201	       col = c("firebrick", "steelblue", "darkgreen"),
   202	       legend = c("IVW", "MR-Egger", "Weighted median"))
   203	mtext("Effects oriented so SNP-exposure effects are positive; bars are 95% CIs", side = 1, line = 4, cex = 0.7)
   204	dev.off()
   205	
   206	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- report.md (<= 200 words)
   207	n_drop <- nrow(dat) - n
   208	fmt <- function(i) sprintf("%.2f (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f)", estimates$estimate[i], estimates$ci_lower[i], estimates$ci_upper[i])
   209	report <- c(
   210	  "# BMI and systolic blood pressure: Mendelian randomization (simulated data)",
   211	  "",
   212	  sprintf("**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.", ""),
   213	  "",
   214	  sprintf("**Data.** %d BMI instruments; %d used after harmonisation (%d dropped for missing outcome data, allele mismatch or ambiguous palindromic strand; see `results/harmonisation_log.csv`).", nrow(dat), n, n_drop),
   215	  "",
   216	  sprintf("**Results.** IVW (random effects): %s mmHg per kg/m2. Weighted median: %s. MR-Egger: %s.", fmt(1), fmt(4), fmt(2)),
   217	  "",
   218	  sprintf("**Heterogeneity and pleiotropy.** Cochran's Q = %.1f on %d df (p = %.2g). MR-Egger intercept = %.3f mmHg (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f).", Q, Q_df, Q_p, eg_int, estimates$ci_lower[3], estimates$ci_upper[3]),
   219	  "",
   220	  "**Caveats.** Results rest on the usual MR assumptions, which these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings."
   221	)
   222	words <- length(strsplit(paste(report, collapse = " "), "\\s+")[[1]])
   223	if (words > 200) warning("report.md has ", words, " words (limit 200)")
   224	writeLines(report, "report.md")
   225	cat("Done. Report words:", words, "\n")
